entries.source: SDK 26.2, MPNowPlayingInfoLanguageOption.h, MP_API(ios(9.0), tvos(9.0), macos(10.12.2), watchos(5.0))
entries.reason: THE RELEASE CARRIES NO SUCH CLASS, at both ends, read CLASS-SCOPED rather than from a name list: tools/corpus/objc-inventory.lua over the armv7 dyld shared caches of 6.1.3 and 4.3 reads MPNowPlayingInfoLanguageOption ABSENT from both. Each read carried its controls in the same run - MPVolumeView and MPMediaPlaylist read PRESENT on both ends, and MPNowPlayingInfoCenter reads PRESENT at 6.1.3 and ABSENT at 4.3, so the reader discriminates rather than answering yes to everything it is shown. The whole-cache selector list (selectors_armv7.txt, 113981 DISTINCT NAMES) could not have decided this: a name is on one line if ANY class anywhere declares it, so a one there says nothing about the owner and only a zero means absence from the release. A class no release has is new code and cannot shadow anything, so there is nothing native for it to be, and `absent` - which is for a row whose answer needs a thing the device lacks - is the wrong word: nothing here needs one. WHAT MAKES IT MORE THAN A DECLARATION is that the release carries the inputs it is built from, read at CLASS level in the same two runs: AVMediaSelectionOption is PRESENT at 6.1.3 with 24 own instance methods including -locale, -mediaType, -hasMediaCharacteristic:, -displaysNonForcedSubtitles and -isPlayable, and AVMediaSelectionGroup is PRESENT with 18 own methods including -options, -allowsEmptySelection and -_defaultOption. So the class is a value holder over state the release really has, and not an invented answer to a question the device cannot answer. The two 'automatic' accessors are answered from the option's own stored TYPE, which is the distinction the header's own comment draws at MPNowPlayingInfoLanguageOption.h:56-73; they are NOT answered from a tag constant, because the header names MPLangaugeOptionAutoLangaugeTag in a comment at :68 and the SDK DECLARES NO SUCH SYMBOL anywhere - grep over the 26.2 MediaPlayer headers finds that name in the one comment and in no declaration - so a comparison against it would not link, and a nil tag means the option is DISABLED per :57-58, which is the opposite of automatic
entries.effect: NSClassFromString answers the class, [MPNowPlayingInfoLanguageOption new] allocates a real object instead of messaging nil, and the five declared accessors read what the caller stored. MPChangeLanguageOptionCommandEvent90.m, already on main, declares an MPNowPlayingInfoLanguageOption * property whose type this file makes real - before it, that property could only ever hold nil

entries.source: SDK 26.2, MPNowPlayingInfoLanguageOption.h, MP_API(ios(9.0), tvos(9.0), macos(10.12.2), watchos(5.0))
entries.reason: read CLASS-SCOPED with tools/corpus/objc-inventory.lua over the armv7 caches of 6.1.3 and 4.3, this class reads ABSENT from both, with the controls named in the MPNowPlayingInfoLanguageOption row in the same two runs - so the zero is the release's and not the reader's. A class no release has is new code and cannot shadow anything, which is what lets it be `implemented` over `absent`. It is built over the same real state as its element class: AVMediaSelectionGroup is PRESENT at 6.1.3 and its own 18 methods include -options and -allowsEmptySelection, the two things this group holds. The header calls it 'a mutually exclusive group of language options' where 'only one language option within a given group may be active at a time' (:86-87), and this object does NOT enforce that: it holds the set the caller built and the one option the caller marked active, because enforcing exclusivity would mean silently dropping options the caller passed, which is a different API from the one Apple declares
entries.effect: NSClassFromString answers the class and a caller-built group holds the options, the default and the allowEmptySelection flag it was given, copied so a later mutation of the caller's array cannot change what the group reads
